question.question:
A project pays an outlay of 160000 USD at time 0 and receives an operating inflow of 20000 USD at the end of each of years 1 to 3. At the end of year 3 it also pays a decommissioning cost of 55000 USD; the year-3 net flow is the inflow minus that cost and may be positive, zero or negative. Inflows are positive, outflows negative. NPV is computed on the net flows at 14 percent per year. For the modified IRR, classify each year's net flow by sign: negative net flows (including the time-0 outlay) are discounted to time 0 at a finance rate of 6.5 percent per year, positive net flows are compounded to the end of year 3 at a reinvestment rate of 12 percent per year, and a zero net flow is ignored. The MIRR is the annual rate that grows that total present value into that total future value over 3 years. Compute the MIRR as a percentage.

Answer format: use exact arithmetic through all intermediate steps, round only the final value half up to 2 decimal digits, and return only the numeric value interpreted in `percent` with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: Net present value of all net cash flows at the stated discount rate
Whether the NPV is strictly positive
Present value at time zero of negative net flows, as a positive magnitude
Total future value at final year of positive net flows at the reinvestment rate
